plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, pendulous clusters of fragrant pea-like flowers. It twines counterclockwise and can cover pergolas, walls, and trees. Flowers appear before or with the emerging leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a century, and the famous Sierra Madre wisteria in California, planted in 1894, covers about an acre and weighs several tons.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers atop sturdy stems and broad blue-green leaves. Late-flowering cultivars are at their peak in late April, after early daffodils and crocuses have faded.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate regions, especially the Netherlands; ancestors native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxurious canal house.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A woodland bulb forming carpets of nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented flowers that droop to one side of an arching stem. It thrives in the dappled light of ancient deciduous woodlands.
plants.location: Native to Western Europe, especially the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, and Spain
plants.funFact: Bluebells are a protected species in the UK, and it is illegal to collect wild bulbs; they can take 5 to 7 years to flower from seed.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, fern-leaved tree that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lilac-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some trees continue blooming into late autumn in warmer areas, while others bloom sporadically; in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, early blooming begins around late April to May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (April to June); primarily October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, Texas, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in Pretoria, South Africa, the tree gives the city the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
